title: Snapshots, pinned solvers and run manifests

questions.stem: A planning tool names each scenario by sha256(str(inputs)), where inputs holds a set of forced-in project ids. Two nightly runs of the same unchanged scenario report different names. What is the most likely cause?

options.text: str of the dict can write its keys in a new order, so the text can change
options.says: The page says str() of a dict follows insertion order, so the same code writes the same text each run.

options.text: sha256 can digest the set's text anew in a new process, so names can change
options.says: A SHA-256 digest depends only on the bytes; equal text gives one digest in every process.

options.text: str of the set can follow each process's hash salt, so the text can change
options.says: Right: the page digested str of one set under two hash seeds and got two digests.

options.text: str can sort the set's ids anew in each process, so the text can change
options.says: str does not sort; and sorted ids digest the same everywhere, as the page's sorted(set) line shows.

origin.section: A Snapshot Is the Digest of the Inputs in One Canonical Form

questions.stem: A team is deciding what goes into each run's manifest, which reruns are compared against byte for byte. Which of these belongs outside it?

options.text: the seconds the solve took on the clock
options.says: Right: wall time varies on every run, so the page keeps it apart under clock.

options.text: the thread count passed to the solver
options.says: The thread count changes the path (10.2.2), so it is an input the manifest records.

options.text: the version of OR-Tools that was installed
options.says: The version fixes MathOpt's HiGHS and SCIP, so the manifest records it.

options.text: the simplex iterations the solve performed
options.says: Work counts repeat when a run repeats and differ first when it does not; the page keeps them.

origin.section: A Run Manifest Records What Went In and What Came Out, and Leaves Out the Clock

questions.stem: A team wants every rerun to use the same HiGHS that MathOpt ran, and pins highspy==1.14.0 in its requirements. What does the page say about that?

options.text: That pin can be enough, since MathOpt runs the HiGHS that pip installed
options.says: MathOpt runs the HiGHS inside the OR-Tools wheel; v9.15 carries HiGHS 1.12.0.

options.text: The ortools pin can matter more, since its wheel carries its own HiGHS
options.says: Right: the OR-Tools version fixes the HiGHS and SCIP that MathOpt runs; highspy is another HiGHS.

options.text: A pin on the system's HiGHS library can do it, since MathOpt loads that
options.says: The page printed libhighs.so.1 among the files the OR-Tools wheel carries.

options.text: Both pins can matter, since highspy and ortools load one HiGHS library
options.says: The page printed highspy as HiGHS packaged on its own, apart from the copy in the OR-Tools wheel.

origin.section: The Solver's Version Is an Input Too: Pin It and Record It
